record.paper_title: Open questions for strongly interacting Fermi gases with zero-range interactions
record.original_question: At the unitary limit of an equal-mass, spin-unpolarized, two-component Fermi gas at zero temperature, what is the sign and value of the acoustic curvature parameter γ in the low-wave-number sound dispersion? This must resolve the conflict between microscopic approximations predicting γ > 0 and a recent Bragg experiment suggesting γ < 0, because the sign determines whether low-temperature collisionless sound damping is governed by three-phonon Beliaev-Landau processes or four-phonon Landau-Khalatnikov processes.

evidence.quote: The situation is much more open for the curvature parameter γ.
The error, however, is uncontrolled, and we’re not even sure of the sign.

The question of the sign of γ at the unitary limit, which crucially determines the three-phonon (γ > 0) or four-phonon ( γ < 0) nature of sound damping in the low-temperature collisionless regime, therefore remains largely open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a three-dimensional, equal-mass, spin-1/2 (two-component, spin-unpolarized) Fermi gas at zero temperature in the unitary limit, i.e. with s-wave scattering length |a| = ∞ and zero-range interactions, so that the ground state is a universal superfluid characterized only by the Fermi momentum k_F (with Fermi energy E_F = ℏ²k_F²/(2m) and sound speed c determined by the Bertsch parameter). Let ω(q) denote the dispersion relation of the Bogoliubov–Anderson phonon branch as a function of the wave number q. Expand at small q in the form

  ω(q) = c q [ 1 + (γ/8) (ℏ q / (m c))² + O(q⁴) ],

which defines the dimensionless acoustic curvature parameter γ. The sign of γ governs the dominant low-temperature collisionless phonon damping mechanism: γ > 0 (convex dispersion) makes three-phonon Beliaev–Landau processes (1 ↔ 2 phonons) kinematically allowed and dominant, while γ < 0 (concave dispersion) forbids them and renders four-phonon Landau–Khalatnikov processes (2 ↔ 2 phonons) dominant.

Determine the sign of γ and its numerical value for the unitary Fermi gas at zero temperature.
artifact.status_search_result: The sign and value of the acoustic curvature γ at unitarity remain disputed. Microscopic approximations (e.g., quasiparticle RPA / pair-fluctuation theories around 2016–2020) yield γ > 0, while a Bragg-spectroscopy experiment (Hoinka et al., PRL 124, 150401 (2020)) reports a concave (γ < 0) branch. No consensus reconciliation has been published; the question is described as largely open in recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: High-Frequency Sound in a Unitary Fermi Gas
status_evidence.snippet: Bragg-spectroscopy measurement of the phonon branch in a unitary Fermi gas reporting a concave dispersion (γ < 0).
status_evidence.claim: Experiment suggests γ < 0 (concave dispersion) at unitarity.

status_evidence.title: Three-phonon and four-phonon interaction processes in a pair-condensed Fermi gas
status_evidence.snippet: When the concavity of the dispersion is upward (γ>0), Beliaev-Landau three-phonon damping dominates; when concave (γ<0), Landau-Khalatnikov four-phonon damping dominates.
status_evidence.claim: The sign of γ determines whether three- or four-phonon damping dominates, and microscopic RPA-type calculations indicate γ > 0 at unitarity.
